(a) Determination of Compensation.—Section 424(b)(2)(E) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act (sec. 1–204.24(b)(2)(E), D.C. Official Code) is amended to read as follows:“(E) Pay.—The Chief Financial Officer shall be paid at a rate such that the total amount of compensation paid during any calendar year does not exceed an amount equal to the limit on total pay which is applicable during the year under section 5307 of title 5, United States Code, to an employee described in section 5307(d) of such title.”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to pay periods beginning on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only sets a cap on the pay of the District of Columbia Chief Financial Officer and gives an effective date. A tempting reading is that the involvement of the District of Columbia (a local government) signals outside-party involvement, but nothing here calls for consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue over a federal decision. It is purely a compensation provision with no participation process.
fable.s: The Chief Financial Officer shall be paid at a rate such that the total amount of compensation paid during any calendar year does not exceed an amount equal to the limit on total pay

opus.w: This section only caps the D.C. Chief Financial Officer's pay and sets when the change takes effect. It does not require any federal decision-maker to consult or coordinate with anyone outside the federal government. The mention of the District of Columbia might look like local-government involvement, but D.C. is not asked to take part in any federal decision. Nothing in the section is on-topic for participation, so the quoted span is empty.
opus.b: **Reasoning.** It's tempting to read this as participation because the District of Columbia is a government outside the federal one. That reading fails. The section is Congress changing how the D.C. Chief Financial Officer's pay is capped and when the change takes effect. No outside party is asked for its views before any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a statutory cap on the compensation of the Chief Financial Officer based on federal pay scales. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before the compensation is determined. The determination is automatic based on the law, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: The Chief Financial Officer shall be paid at a rate such that the total amount of compensation paid during any calendar year does not exceed an amount equal to the limit on total pay which is applicable during the year under section 5307 of title 5, United States Code, to an employee described in section 5307(d) of such title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that setting a pay cap based on a federal statute involves some form of coordination or consultation with federal standards. However, this is merely a statutory definition of a salary limit for a local official. There is no requirement for the Chief Financial Officer, the District government, or any outside party to consult with the federal government, the public, or any advisory body before the pay is determined. The "participation" definition requires interaction with people *outside* the government before a decision is made. Here, the decision (the pay rate) is mechanically determined by a formula in the law, with no interactive process involving outsiders.
